chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid from Burayd al-Ajli said:

I asked him about a man who manumitted his slave by contract (muqatadah) for one thousand dirhams, and did not stipulate at the time of contracting that if he became unable to pay the remainder, he would return to slavery. And that the muqatadah paid to his master five hundred dirhams, then the muqatadah died, leaving wealth and a mature son. He said: Half of whatever the muqatadah left is for his master who contracted with him, and the remaining half is for the son of the muqatadah, because the muqatadah died, half of him was free and half was a slave to the one who contracted with him. So the son of the muqatadah is like his father: half free and half a slave to the one who contracted with his father. If he pays to the one who contracted with his father what remained on his father, then he is free, and there is no claim of anyone among the people upon him.

key_terms.رَدٌّ فِي الرَّقِّ: Return to slavery (if unable to pay)
key_terms.مكاتبة: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum in installments
key_terms.مكاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract of manumission
key_terms.نِصْفُهُ حُرٌّ وَنِصْفُهُ عَبْدٌ: Half free and half slave (status of the muqatadah)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance distribution for a muqatadah who dies with an unpaid balance?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar elucidates the unique legal status of the *muqatadah* (slave contracted for manumission), establishing that upon death, the estate is divided such that half goes to the master and half to the son, mirroring the father's half-free, half-slave status. It further clarifies that the son inherits this same fractional status and can secure full emancipation by settling the remaining debt, a principle rooted in the Quranic injunction to grant freedom to those who pay their manumission dues.
